verses.text: In Iconium, Paul and Barnabas went together into the Jewish synagogue and spoke so effectively that many Jews and Greeks believed.
But the Jews who refused to believe stirred up the Gentiles and turned them against the believers.
So Paul and Barnabas stayed there a long time, speaking boldly for the Lord. The Lord confirmed his message of grace by enabling them to perform signs and wonders.
The city’s people split into two sides: some supported the Jews, others the apostles.
Then some Gentiles and Jews, together with their leaders, planned to mistreat and stone them.
When Paul and Barnabas learned about it, they fled to the Lycaonian cities of Lystra and Derbe and the surrounding area.
There they kept announcing the Good News.
In Lystra there was a man who couldn’t use his feet. He had been lame from birth and had never walked.
He listened to Paul speaking. Paul looked closely at him and saw that he had faith to be healed.
Paul called out, “Stand up straight on your feet!” The man jumped up and began walking.
When the crowd saw what Paul had done, they shouted in the Lycaonian language, “The gods have come down to us looking like people!”
They called Barnabas Jupiter and Paul Mercury, since Paul did most of the speaking.
The priest of Jupiter, whose temple stood in front of the city, brought oxen and flower garlands to the gates. He and the crowd wanted to offer sacrifices to them.
When the apostles Barnabas and Paul heard about it, they tore their clothes and rushed into the crowd, shouting:

“People, why are you doing this? We’re human beings just like you. We bring you Good News so you’ll turn away from these worthless things and turn to the living God, who made the sky, the earth, the sea, and everything in them.
“In past generations he allowed all nations to go their own way.
“Yet he never left himself without a witness: he did good, sent rain from heaven, gave fruitful seasons, and filled you with food and gladness.”
Even with these words, they could barely stop the crowd from sacrificing to them.
Then some Jews came from Antioch and Iconium and persuaded the crowd. They stoned Paul and dragged him outside the city, thinking he was dead.
But when the disciples gathered around him, he got up and went back into the city. The next day he left with Barnabas for Derbe.
After announcing the Good News in Derbe and making many disciples, they returned to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch.
They encouraged the disciples to stay strong in the faith, saying, “We must go through many troubles to enter God’s Kingdom.”
They appointed elders for them in every church. After praying and fasting, they entrusted them to the Lord, in whom they had believed.
They traveled through Pisidia and came to Pamphylia.
After speaking the word in Perga, they went down to Attalia.
From there they sailed to Antioch, where they had first been entrusted to God’s grace for the work they had now completed.
When they arrived, they gathered the church and reported everything God had done through them, including how he had opened the door of faith to the Gentiles.
They stayed there with the disciples for a long time.
